audit.whatIsWrong: The whole matchup is framed around Miasma's grounding. breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t both name Miasma as 'matchup-defining' and explain it as 'Grounds you — dashes and movement abilities are disabled inside it'. whys[2] says 'grounding W cancels any gap-close'.
audit.why: Nasus has no dash, no blink and no movement ability. Siphoning Strike is an attack modifier, Wither is a targeted slow, Spirit Fire is a ground-targeted zone and Fury of the Sands is a self-buff. Miasma's grounding component does nothing to his kit, and 'cancels any gap-close' describes a gap-close he does not have. Building the page's matchup-defining ability on a mechanic that cannot affect this champion is precisely the non-interaction the relevance rule exists to prevent — and it costs the slot that should hold the fact that actually decides the lane.
audit.corrected: Moved matchup-defining status to Petrifying Gaze and its facing rule. Kept Miasma where it genuinely matters to Nasus — as her longest cooldown at 24s rank 1, i.e. his walk-up window — rather than for the grounding.

audit.whatIsWrong: Petrifying Gaze is called 'R face-stun' four times, but the facing rule itself is never stated anywhere.
audit.why: Riot's text: it stuns 'any enemies in front of her that are facing her' and merely slows 'any others with their back turned'. Turning around and walking away converts a long stun into a slow. For a champion as slow and as commit-dependent as Nasus this is the difference between surviving her ultimate and dying to the follow-up, and it is the single most valuable sentence available in the matchup. The shorthand 'face-stun' gestures at the mechanic without ever telling the player what to do about it.
audit.corrected: Stated the turn-away counterplay explicitly in content.mid, content.late, whys[6], spikes[3], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two places invert who Miasma grounds: whys[5] says 'run her grounded body down' and spikes[2] says 'land an empowered Q burst once she's grounded'.
audit.why: Miasma grounds Cassiopeia's enemies, not Cassiopeia. Both lines tell the player to wait for a state that never happens, which means waiting forever for a window that will not come.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both around conditions that do occur — Wither landing, and Miasma being spent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twin Fang is never mentioned in either layer, despite being the ability that does most of her damage and all of her sustain.
audit.why: Twin Fang has a 0.75s cooldown, heals her for a percentage of damage dealt, and deals increased damage specifically to POISONED targets. That last clause is the whole matchup: Noxious Blast is the enabler and Twin Fang is the payoff, so a Nasus who avoids the poison faces a much weaker ability. The guide describes her damage as generic 'poison ticks' and so never gives the player the lever.
audit.corrected: Named Twin Fang and stated the poison dependency in content.early, whys[2], phases[2].why and dontsFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere', sequencingCues = 0. No Cassiopeia cooldown number appears in either layer.
audit.why: Her cooldowns are wildly asymmetric and that asymmetry is the sequencing: Twin Fang 0.75s, Noxious Blast 3.5s, Miasma 24/22/20/18/16s. Waiting for Twin Fang or Noxious Blast is pointless — they are always up. Miasma is the only thing worth counting, and at 24s at rank 1 it is a genuinely long window.
audit.corrected: Added Miasma's 24s as the walk-up trigger in content.mid, spikes[2], dosFull[2].d and report[5].t, and the 0.75s/poison-dependency for Twin Fang.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds source in the item block, in a matchup flagged needs-antiheal.
audit.why: Twin Fang heals her for a percentage of the damage it deals and fires roughly every 0.75s, so her sustain scales with how long the fight lasts. The stated Nasus plan is to win exactly those long fights after two items.
audit.corrected: Added Executioner's Calling, trimming the redundant Sheen sentence the Trinity Force entry already implies.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] is titled 'Wither him the moment Miasma is down' — Cassiopeia is female, and the same 'him' appears in report[5].t. dontsFull[1] titled 'Stack greedily without vision' carries the same paste-error description found on all six previous matchups.
audit.why: Seven of seven matchups audited in this slice carry the dontsFull[1].d defect, confirming it as a template-level bug. The pronoun error is cosmetic but appears in a card title, which is the most visible text on the page.
audit.corrected: Fixed the pronoun and rewrote both descriptions to match their titles.

audit.why: 49.66% over 294 games, and the chart [Skill, Cassiopeia x3, Skill, Nasus, Nasus] is the most honest one in this slice — it gives her the early lane, marks level 6 as skill, and flips at first item. It matches the win rate and no contradiction was flagged.

edits.before: Cassiopeia's poison (Q) plus her grounding W is the early game — she chip-pokes you off the wave before you have Wither to answer, so don't walk up for a Q stack you'll pay double for in poison damage. Last-hit with the tip of your Spirit Fire (E) and let Soul Eater lifesteal heal the poison ticks. You concede these levels — that's fine, you're a juggernaut, just don't die to a full poison rotation chasing a stack.
edits.after: Noxious Blast is the early game — it poisons you, and Twin Fang only does its big damage to a poisoned target, so breaking that chain collapses her output. She chip-pokes you off the wave before Wither answers, so don't walk up for a Q stack you'll pay double for. Last-hit with the tip of your Spirit Fire and let Soul Eater lifesteal heal the ticks. You concede these levels — just don't die to a full rotation chasing a stack.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still hers — she's poison-stacking and kiting you with no-boots passive move speed while you hoard Q stacks and play not to die. At 6 your Fury of the Sands plus Wither finally lets you survive or punish a committed all-in: if she burns her R face-stun or steps up to poke, W her, eat the slow on her attack speed, and Spirit Fire her feet for the armor shred. Don't chase past tower into her grounding — bait the cooldowns instead.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still hers — she's poison-stacking and kiting you with Serpentine Grace move speed while you hoard Q stacks and play not to die. At 6, Petrifying Gaze only stuns targets that are facing her: turn and walk away and you take a slow instead of a stun. That one habit decides the matchup. If she burns it or steps up to poke, Wither her and Spirit Fire her feet for the shred. Miasma is 24s at rank 1 — walk up on that.

notes: HIGH-VALUE UNVERIFIED, worth a wiki pass before anything else in this matchup: whether Miasma's grounding blocks Flash. If it does, then Miasma into Petrifying Gaze is a guaranteed death sentence for a Nasus with no other escape, and the grounding becomes genuinely matchup-defining after all — which would partly vindicate the framing I just moved away from. needsResearch.flashBuffer is null for both champions and Riot's text says only 'Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities', which does not settle whether a summoner spell counts. I deliberately made no claim either way. What I could establish is that the grounding does nothing to Nasus's own kit — he has no dash, blink or movement ability — which is why I moved the matchup-defining slot to Petrifying Gaze's facing rule, a fact that is unambiguous in Riot's text and immediately actionable. Also left alone: 'no-boots passive move speed' in content.mid. Cassiopeia being unable to buy boots is not in the kit file, so I neither confirmed nor removed it; I only replaced the phrase where I was rewriting the sentence anyway and kept the claim out of new text. No WKM_LINES problems seen for this pairing.
